run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-16T09:43:20Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend is explained by frontend's own failing outbound calls to product-catalog. frontend's error-span rate moved from a flat 0 baseline (0 at every step from 09:23:20 through 09:42:20) to 1.72/s at 09:43:20, peaked at 23.22/s at 09:48:20 and was still 17.68/s at 09:52:20; its largest failing operations are client span grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct (2.57/s) paired with server GET /api/products/{productId} (2.57/s), with smaller contributions from RecommendationService/ListRecommendations (0.47/s), CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (0.38/s) and tcp.connect (0.04/s). The dependency itself is broken: Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog carries a container command override of ["invalid-command"]; its new ReplicaSet product-catalog-fcf7564cf was created 2026-11-16T09:41:29Z with the same image (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog) as the previous ReplicaSet product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc but with that command, and container start fails at init with 'exec: "invalid-command": executable file not found in $PATH' (StartError, exitCode 128, 5 restarts, CrashLoopBackOff, ready=false). product-catalog's span rate fell from ~10.5 spans/s to 0 and its Endpoints object holds only notReadyAddresses, so callers have no ready backend. recommendation (2.00 error spans/s on /oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts and get_product_list) and checkout (1.24/s on oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct and CheckoutService/PlaceOrder) show their own error spans from the same dependency, and frontend-proxy reports its own errors on ingress (7.07/s) and router frontend egress (7.06/s). cart, ad, accounting, payment and fraud-detection emitted no error spans, and every other pod is ready with 0 restarts.

claims.text: frontend had a zero error-span baseline and then a sustained error-span rate: sum by status_code over traces_span_metrics_calls_total for service_name=frontend was 0 for STATUS_CODE_ERROR at every step from 09:23:20 to 09:42:20, then 1.7222/s at 09:43:20, peaked at 23.2239/s at 09:48:20 and was 17.6842/s at 09:52:20, while STATUS_CODE_UNSET fell from ~45/s to ~13/s.
At 09:45:00 frontend's error spans were 14.4388/s and its STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans 36.9185/s (sum by status_code), so the service was actively emitting error spans when the alert fired.

frontend's error spans at 09:45:00 break down by span_name as: GET 3.7444/s, grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct 2.5687/s with GET /api/products/{productId} 2.5687/s and executing api route (pages) /api/products/[productId] 2.5687/s, grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations 0.4739/s with GET /api/recommendations 0.4739/s, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 0.3815/s with POST /api/checkout 0.3815/s and POST 0.3815/s, and tcp.connect 0.0407/s; the cart, ad and /api/data operations were 0.

In the 1-minute rate series the first non-zero value for frontend error spans is at 09:42:45 (15.5/s), after which the sampled evaluations hold ~47.9-51.2/s; the resolution-15s series is sparse (some steps read 0), so the exact first failed request is not resolved.

Pod product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l (owner ReplicaSet product-catalog-fcf7564cf) is phase Running but Ready=False and ContainersReady=False: restartCount 5, started false, state waiting CrashLoopBackOff ('back-off 2m40s restarting failed container=product-catalog'), lastState terminated reason StartError exitCode 128 finishedAt 2026-11-16T09:44:59Z with message 'failed to create containerd task: ... exec: "invalid-command": executable file not found in $PATH'.

The product-catalog Deployment spec sets containers[0].command to ["invalid-command"] for image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog (args null, containerPort 8080), and its status shows spec.replicas 1, updatedReplicas 1, unavailableReplicas 1.

The change was configuration-only, not an image change: ReplicaSet product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc has image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog with command null and replicas 0, while ReplicaSet product-catalog-fcf7564cf (created 2026-11-16T09:41:29Z, owner product-catalog) has the same image with command ["invalid-command"] and replicas 1.

product-catalog events show the replacement sequence inside the window: Scheduled 09:41:29, Created and Failed (invalid-command) and BackOff on product-catalog-fcf7564cf-2fvnx at 09:41:33-09:41:34, Killing and SuccessfulDelete of the old pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-wzpwm at 09:41:38, SuccessfulCreate of product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l at 09:41:46, then repeated 'Error: ... exec: "invalid-command": executable file not found in $PATH' (count 6) and BackOff (count 25) up to 09:47:41.

Among all ReplicaSets in otel-demo created after 09:00, product-catalog-fcf7564cf (09:41:29, command ["invalid-command"]) is the only one whose pod template carries that command; the ReplicaSets created at 09:11-09:13 have command null except the two flagd ones.

Endpoints object product-catalog in otel-demo contains only notReadyAddresses (100.96.2.148, targetRef pod product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l, port tcp-service 8080), i.e. no ready backend; the Service selects opentelemetry.io/name=product-catalog on port 8080 targetPort 8080 with clusterIP 100.64.32.100.

product-catalog stopped emitting spans over the same period: sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="product-catalog"}[5m])) held ~10.24-10.94 spans/s from 09:28:20 to 09:41:20, then 8.5444 at 09:43:20, 5.8556, 3.2074, 0.3407, and 0 from 09:47:20 onward.

recommendation and checkout produced their own error spans at 09:48:00: recommendation 2.0037/s total, on span_name /oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts 1/s, get_product_list 1/s and /flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream 0.0037/s; checkout 1.2444/s total, on span_name oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct 0.6222/s and oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 0.6222/s.
Per-service error-span rates at 09:48:00 were frontend 28.2296/s, frontend-proxy 14.1333/s, recommendation 2.0037/s, checkout 1.2444/s, and 0 for accounting, fraud-detection, ad and payment.
frontend-proxy's own error spans at 09:48:00 are on span_name 'ingress' (7.0704/s) and 'router frontend egress' (7.0630/s), i.e. on its traffic toward frontend rather than on a separate backend.

This is not a cluster-wide or node-wide failure: every other otel-demo pod listed is Running and ready with restartCount 0 (including frontend-675fd7b5c5-9f6l5, recommendation-5f45f75855-xrpch, checkout-5dccddf8bb-8fzjm, cart-755465879b-4tgpm, ad-554b849958-bhrzb, flagd-8556f87d4b-kkf6p); product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l is the only pod with ready=false.

cart and ad were not failing at 09:48:00 despite carrying traffic: cart emitted 14.8111/s STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans and ad 2.2852/s UNSET with 0 error spans, while product-catalog emitted 0 spans of any status, so the error signal is specific to product-catalog-dependent paths rather than general to the namespace.

The flagd rollout was considered as an alternative cause and rejected for this alert: two flagd ReplicaSets were created at 09:11:30 and 09:13:32, roughly 28-30 minutes before the 09:43:20 alert onset, the flagd pod is ready with restartCount 0, and the only error span tied to flagd is recommendation's client span /flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream at 0.0037/s, orders of magnitude below frontend's error rate.

frontend being itself broken (rather than failing on a dependency) is not supported: pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-9f6l5 is Running, ready with restartCount 0, and its error spans are concentrated on outbound client operations (grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct 2.5687/s, grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations 0.4739/s, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 0.3815/s) plus the tcp.connect span (0.0407/s), not on an internal frontend operation.

The path the evidence supports is: the Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog pod template command override ["invalid-command"] made the new ReplicaSet's container fail at init (StartError, exit 128), the single replica never became ready, Endpoints product-catalog kept only notReadyAddresses, and callers' ProductCatalog gRPC calls (frontend GetProduct, recommendation ListProducts, checkout GetProduct) began returning errors, which frontend surfaced as its own error spans and frontend-proxy recorded as ingress and router frontend egress errors; a trace-level parent-child confirmation of this edge was not obtainable.

Restore the product-catalog Deployment pod template to the image's default entrypoint (remove the containers[0].command ["invalid-command"] override, e.g. by reverting the change that produced ReplicaSet product-catalog-fcf7564cf), then confirm the new pod reaches Ready and that Endpoints product-catalog gains a ready address before expecting frontend, recommendation and checkout error spans to clear.

gaps: The frontend->product-catalog call edge is inferred from span-metric operation names only: Jaeger trace queries for service frontend in 09:43:20-09:52:52 returned no traces (traces_search view 27ff02d7-468f-44ea-b006-f679abee8c77-t0:fa1da9d2-5a1c-4925-a07e-74fcbc86cc15 and traces_search_by_tags view ff33c56f-6f43-442c-9012-c74e7d0c2713-t0:7cab4b69-96df-47e8-a2dc-32ca71f93aaa both status no_data), so parent references could not be checked.

Container logs could not corroborate: fetch_pod_logs for frontend-675fd7b5c5-9f6l5 returned no lines (views b2955ec9-29c2-416c-b547-0c306ed2260f-t1:29057d2b-75b0-4eb2-9668-b1e23d21835e and ff33c56f-6f43-442c-9012-c74e7d0c2713-t1:c91b3ecd-0be5-46eb-8c02-2926e687ef50, status no_data) and for product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l returned no lines with no previous instance (view 71bf1afb-2d36-49f4-b0a7-298fb29025e9-t1:cceaecdb-5706-46e9-a99d-9a2ec2b37184, status no_data); application-level error text therefore remains unverified.

kube-state-metrics series are absent from this Prometheus (get_metric_names {__name__=~"kube_.*"} view 5d50b8c4-865b-4e23-a0d6-121da38b36b6-t0:41d7445a-cfb9-4388-8034-c8a522cbbd38 and kube_pod_container_info view 5d50b8c4-865b-4e23-a0d6-121da38b36b6-t1:b5b9f9aa-3274-48d4-9c2e-42fd3da0d717, both status no_data), and kube_deployment_status_replicas_available returned nothing (view d2ff0984-c1c2-405f-931a-e92eedd1d729-t1:c1377ba8-252f-4bf5-8dc8-5f6c8f93165b, status no_data), so no available/ready-replica baseline exists and rollout facts rest on ReplicaSet objects and events.

The alerting rule RequestErrorRate was not returned by list_prometheus_rules (view 9a7a8bef-224d-43e8-8f78-9ec11357fccf-t0:6a8da1ae-5f75-4200-aad7-c0ff6f89d776, status no_data), so the alert's exact expression, window and threshold were not verified and the annotation value 16.8667 was not matched to a specific expression.

HTTP request-level metric labels could not be inspected: get_label_values for status_code matching http_server_request_duration_seconds_count on service_name=frontend returned nothing (view b16f7354-3dfb-4fee-bf9f-fff8bc210379-t1:16f9dabe-bb80-4eff-a006-2b77edca7c46, status no_data).
The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so who or what applied the product-catalog command override (commit, pipeline or manual edit) is unknown.

Timing is not fully resolved: the pod first failed at 09:41:34-09:41:38, but the 5-minute frontend error rate was still 0 at 09:42:20 and the first non-zero 1-minute value is 09:42:45; scrape sparsity is the likely explanation but the exact first failed request time is unknown.

The concurrent frontend traffic drop (STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans from ~45/s to ~13/s) was not explained; whether load-generator behaviour changed or frontend simply served fewer successful requests was not verified.
next_steps: Have a human confirm the origin of the product-catalog Deployment change at 09:41:29 (change_history is not integrated here) and revert the containers[0].command override to the image default entrypoint.

After the rollout, verify pod product-catalog-fcf7564cf-* is Ready with restartCount 0 and that Endpoints product-catalog lists a ready address, then re-check frontend, recommendation and checkout error-span rates against the pre-incident zero baseline.
Review the admission/CI path that allowed a non-existent command to be applied to a pod template, since the failure was caught only by readiness and alerting rather than by validation.
Restore or extend Jaeger coverage for the otel-demo namespace so trace-level confirmation of the frontend -> product-catalog edge is available during incidents.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
